title: Borda Score and Borda Winner
body_html:
Borda Score and Borda Winner

The Borda score of an alternative $a$ under preference $P_i$ counts how many alternatives are ranked strictly below $a$: $$ b(P_i, a) = \#\{c \in A \mid a \succ_{P_i} c\}. $$

The total Borda score across the profile is $$ B(P, a) = \sum_{i \in N} b(P_i, a). $$

An alternative $a$ is a Borda winner if it maximizes the total Borda score: $$ \forall c \in A,\ B(P, c) \le B(P, a). $$

In Lean: SocialChoice.Voting.bordaScore, .bordaTotalScore, and .IsBordaWinner. The definitions live under noncomputable because filtering by a bare-Prop strict preference uses classical decidability.

Ties between Borda winners are explicitly allowed — IsBordaWinner is the $\arg\max$ membership predicate, not a function returning a unique winner.

Properties (informal)

  • Borda is monotonic, anonymous, and neutral.
  • Borda is not a Condorcet method ([[social_choice.voting.condorcet_winner]]): the Borda winner may differ from the Condorcet winner when both exist.
  • Borda is strategy-manipulable ([[social_choice.voting.strategyproof]] fails) — already follows from Gibbard–Satterthwaite for $|A| \ge 3$.

References

  • [AGT Chapter 10] Nisan, Roughgarden, Tardos, and Vazirani, Algorithmic Game Theory, references/AlgorithmicGameTheory.pdf. Positional scoring rules.
